results.question: How many monitoring samples are in the dataset?
results.generated_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS sample_count FROM device_metrics;

results.question: How many devices does each site have? Sort by site name.
results.generated_sql:
SELECT s.name AS site_name, COUNT(d.id) AS device_count
FROM sites s
LEFT JOIN devices d ON s.id = d.site_id
GROUP BY s.name
ORDER BY s.name
LIMIT 100;

results.question: Which devices recorded CPU above 80%, and how many such samples did each have? Sort by hostname.
results.generated_sql:
SELECT d.hostname, COUNT(*) AS high_cpu_samples
FROM device_metrics dm
JOIN devices d ON dm.device_id = d.id
WHERE dm.cpu_pct > 80
GROUP BY d.hostname
ORDER BY d.hostname
LIMIT 100;

results.question: How many samples exceeded 80% CPU on November 3, 2026 UTC?
results.generated_sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS high_cpu_samples
FROM device_metrics
WHERE cpu_pct > 80
  AND collected_at >= '2026-11-03 00:00:00'
  AND collected_at < '2026-11-04 00:00:00';

results.question: Which devices have monitoring samples on November 8, 2026 UTC? Sort by hostname.
results.generated_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT d.hostname
FROM device_metrics dm
JOIN devices d ON dm.device_id = d.id
WHERE dm.collected_at >= '2026-11-08 00:00:00'
  AND dm.collected_at < '2026-11-09 00:00:00'
ORDER BY d.hostname
LIMIT 100;

scope: Five development examples on synthetic data; not held-out accuracy.
